title: Jade Belwyn [LORA/Krea 2]
description:

It gives images his muted sepia and parchment tones, with soft brushwork and a pencil underdrawing that often shows through. Characters come out as big-eyed, doll-like girls with tiny noses and sharp, theatrical expressions. They wear Victorian and circus-style costumes: top hats, bonnets, ruffled collars and corsets. Odd small creatures and spindly ornaments tend to drift around them. The overall feel is old and slightly faded, like a storybook painting from another century with something a little wrong in it.

Trigger word: BdtPtrsStl

Usage

  • Put the trigger word first, then describe a character, outfit and setting.

  • Start at strength 0.6–1.4.

  • Portraits and single full-figure characters work best, since most of the training paintings show one figure.

- Base model path: 50 steps, CFG 1, euler/simple, denoise 1.0 - the highest-quality setting before distilled shortcuts
- Multi-image reference support through ReferenceMultiLatent and BatchImagesNode: feed up to 10 references and address them as ref_image_0, ref_image_1, ...

title: Katherine Roccabruna [LORA/ZImageTurbo]
description:
This LoRA does not depict a real person; it is a fictional creation.

Katherine Roccabruna grew up in the RoccaBruna family of Florence, surrounded by palazzos that were already lessons in furniture. 🌟 Stone, proportion, and the way a chair changes a conversation were household knowledge. She sketches because the hand still knows things a screen rushes past. The city remains both client and teacher.

As a furniture designer she builds pieces that have to hold a body and a story at the same time. 🎨 A table begins as a drawing, then as wood chosen at a market, then as a stubborn round of joinery. Florentine elegance and a modern line argue until they agree. She cares whether a drawer will still run smoothly in ten years. 🪑 The workshop smells of timber and varnish, and the afternoon disappears into that smell on purpose.

Evening might be a cafe sketch or a walk with no pencil at all. ☕🇮🇹 She likes seeing other people's rooms lit up, each one a small museum of choices.

description:
MOSS-Image SFT can produce noticeable vertical color banding, particularly in skies, gradients, fog, and large areas of uniform color.

These two weight-difference adapters reduce the artifact by restoring selected transformer layers to their MOSS-Image Base weights, without requiring a full replacement checkpoint.

Main (L37–41) provides the standard correction and can be used on its own at strength 1.0.

Extra (L32–36) extends the correction when stacked with Main, also at strength 1.0. Using both produces the stronger DeBand+ configuration.

The included ComfyUI workflow provides presets for different quality and speed configurations.

These files use ComfyUI's full-rank .diff format rather than conventional low-rank LoRA matrices. Use a compatible ComfyUI loader.
